old_title: MigGPT: Automating the version migration of out-of-tree Linux kernel patches
old_abstract_summary: MigGPT uses code fingerprints and retrieval context to migrate out-of-tree Linux kernel patches across versions. Its benchmark covers real patch projects and measures migration completion against vanilla LLMs.
old_conclusion_summary: The authors report improved patch migration accuracy, but the demonstrated goal is compatibility and maintenance rather than security repair.
old_score_rationale: It automates Linux-kernel maintenance without a security-specific evaluation.
proposed_correction_or_check: Published NeurIPS paper section 6.1 reports a 350-instance CVE patch-backporting benchmark, in addition to general out-of-tree kernel migration; Table 5 reports semantic match. Reassess relevance and check exact benchmark scope; retain version-specific results.

old_title: KEN/Kgent: Kernel Extensions Large Language Model Agent for eBPF
old_abstract_summary: Kgent converts natural-language requests into eBPF kernel extensions and combines LLM comprehension with symbolic execution and feedback to check semantic alignment. The focus is program generation, not security analysis.
old_conclusion_summary: The authors conclude that feedback and symbolic checks improve generated eBPF program alignment, without evaluating an OS-security task.
old_score_rationale: It generates kernel-extension code, but does not evaluate vulnerability detection or OS security.
proposed_correction_or_check: KEN is the earlier arXiv version of Kgent, identified by the authors repository. L041 and C0130 should share one study ID. Evaluate generated eBPF correctness separately from security outcomes.

old_title: Kgent: Kernel Extensions Large Language Model Agent
old_abstract_summary: Kgent translates natural-language requests into eBPF kernel extensions and validates generated code using symbolic execution and iterative feedback. The reported prototype improves correctness over a GPT-4 baseline for kernel-extension generation.
old_score_rationale: It generates code for Linux kernel extensions, an OS-component workflow that could benefit from security validation, but security is not the evaluated task.
proposed_correction_or_check: Published Kgent version of KEN; preserve both record IDs but assign a single study ID. The primary evaluation concerns eBPF generation and correctness.

old_title: kAgent: An execution-guided crash resolution agent for the Linux kernel
old_abstract_summary: kAgent analyzes Syzkaller crash reports, forms execution-grounded hypotheses, generates candidate Linux-kernel repairs, and validates them by reproducing crashes. The study covers benchmark and selected real-world crashes.
old_conclusion_summary: The authors report a crash-resolution workflow for kernel bugs, but the security significance of the evaluated crashes is not isolated.
old_score_rationale: Kernel crash repair is OS-adjacent, but the evidence does not establish a security-specific evaluation.
proposed_correction_or_check: CrashFixer and kAgent share arXiv ID 2504.20412; the current version studies execution-guided kernel crash resolution. The security significance of individual crashes requires separate checking.

old_title: Selene: First Project-Level Automated Proof Benchmark based on seL4 microkernel
old_abstract_summary: Selene introduces an automated proof benchmark based on the seL4 microkernel and evaluates LLMs on project-level proof generation. It studies formal proof assistance rather than security-property verification.
old_conclusion_summary: The benchmark explores proof automation on seL4-derived tasks, but the evaluated properties are not OS-security claims.
old_score_rationale: This is foundational proof-generation research with seL4 context but no security-property evaluation.
proposed_correction_or_check: L040 names the same published ACL Selene study with a descriptive title. The study benchmarks LLM proof generation using seL4; distinguish functional correctness from independently demonstrated security properties.

old_title: Static Detection of Filesystem Vulnerabilities in Android Systems
old_abstract_summary: PathSentinel combines static analysis, Android access-control reasoning, and constraint solving to detect filesystem path traversal, hijacking, and luring vulnerabilities. LLM-generated exploit activities help validate candidate issues on Android devices.
old_conclusion_summary: The study reports direct Android filesystem vulnerability detection and validation, making its evidence OS-specific.
old_score_rationale: It uses LLM support in a security analysis of Android filesystem and access-control behavior.
proposed_correction_or_check: PathSentinel uses static program and access-control analysis to detect Android filesystem vulnerabilities; it uses an LLM downstream to generate exploit/test activities from payloads. Do not attribute all 51 detections to the LLM; assess whether the Android apps and policy target meets the explicit OS scope.
